shared_context.topic: safe amount of Advil to take at one time
shared_context.condition: pain or fever dosing in adults

atoms.1: The recommended dose of ibuprofen varies depending on the individual's age, weight, and medical condition.
atoms.2: Ibuprofen is the active ingredient in Advil.
atoms.3: For adults, the typical dose of ibuprofen is 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours as needed.
atoms.4: Adults should not exceed 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours.
atoms.5: It is essential to consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice regarding ibuprofen use.
atoms.6: Excessive use of ibuprofen can lead to adverse effects such as stomach ulcers, kidney damage, and increased risk of heart attack and stroke.
atoms.7: Taking more than 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours is not recommended for adults.
atoms.8: Taking more than 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours may increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and other complications.
atoms.9: Taking more than 800 mg of ibuprofen at one time is not advised.
atoms.10: Taking more than 800 mg of ibuprofen at one time can lead to increased risk of stomach ulcers and other adverse effects.
atoms.11: Individuals with kidney disease should consult their healthcare provider before taking ibuprofen.
atoms.12: Individuals with liver disease should consult their healthcare provider before taking ibuprofen.
atoms.13: Individuals with stomach ulcers should consult their healthcare provider before taking ibuprofen.
atoms.14: Individuals with certain medical conditions may require a lower dose or alternative medication for ibuprofen.

snippets.output: The recommended dose of ibuprofen varies depending on an individual's age, weight, and medical condition.
Ibuprofen is the active ingredient in Advil.
For adults, the typical dose of ibuprofen is 200–400 mg every 4–6 hours as needed.
Adults should not exceed 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours.
It is essential to consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice regarding ibuprofen use.
Excessive use of ibuprofen can lead to adverse effects such as stomach ulcers, kidney damage, and an increased risk of heart attack and stroke.
Taking more than 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours is not recommended for adults.
Taking more than 1200 mg of ibuprofen in 24 hours may increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and other complications.
Taking more than 800 mg of ibuprofen at one time is not advised.
Taking more than 800 mg of ibuprofen at one time can increase the risk of stomach ulcers and other adverse effects.
Individuals with kidney disease should consult their healthcare provider before taking ibuprofen.
Individuals with liver disease should consult their healthcare provider before taking Advil (ibuprofen).
Individuals with stomach ulcers should consult their healthcare provider before taking Advil (ibuprofen).
Individuals with certain medical conditions may require a lower dose or alternative medication for Advil (ibuprofen).
